name: Procurement Versus Lifecycle Cost
trigger_conditions: lifecycle economics could differ from first-cost logic
anti_triggers: replacement remains valid after maintenance review
physical_basis: Asset stress, weak maintenance and operating discipline can distort the apparent case for replacement or procurement.
operational_basis: Teams can optimize for first-cost procurement before they bound lifecycle economics and maintenance reality.
financial_mechanism: First-cost procurement can misallocate capital if lifecycle cost is governed by maintenance, downtime or operating discipline.
typical_false_assumption: If procurement looks attractive, lifecycle economics must already be bounded.
hypothesis: Procurement logic may be outrunning lifecycle-cost discrimination, making replacement-first action premature.
rival_hypotheses: replacement remains the dominant lever after lifecycle review
minimum_evidence_to_confirm: lifecycle economics materially diverge from procurement-first framing
maintenance or reliability burden remains under-discriminated
falsification_conditions: replacement remains valid after maintenance review
allowed_claim_language: Procurement may be optimizing the wrong variable if lifecycle cost has not yet been bounded.
prohibited_claim_language: The right answer is equipment replacement.
stop_conditions: procurement and lifecycle-cost logic are bounded enough to rank the dominant lever
escalation_conditions: operations or maintenance leadership confirmation required if lifecycle evidence remains thin
claim_permissions_impact: block procurement-driven ROI framing without lifecycle discrimination
example_outputs: Procurement may be optimizing first cost before lifecycle cost is bounded.
tests: manufacturing acceptance bundle should activate this when procurement logic appears before lifecycle economics are bounded
pattern must remain bounded at L2
